issues.title: Advertised embedding exponent range

failure_location.quote: Our main result demonstrates that if the growth rate of a Banach hypothesis space's metric entropy can be bounded by a polynomial function of the radius of the balls, then the hypothesis space can be embedded into a $\mathcal{L}_p$-type Reproducing Kernel Banach space for some $1 \leq p \leq 2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that polynomial metric-entropy growth yields an embedding into an L_p-type RKBS for some p in [1,2]. The old paper's main formal result instead yields an L_s-type RKBS for s>p under p≥2, so its supported target exponent is strictly above 2. The unavailable low-exponent regime is the material difference.
issues.overall_effect: The introduction materially misstates the exponent regime of the paper's central embedding guarantee, although the formal theorem itself is not changed by this prose repair.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the introductory claim by the theorem-supported statement: under the stated entropy bound with exponent p≥2, the paper establishes an embedding into an L_s-type RKBS for every s>p, so only target exponents strictly above 2 are proved. Remove the claim that an exponent in [1,2] is available; retaining that regime would require a new central embedding result.
issues.why_classification: The interval [1,2] is a coherent and substantial advertised target regime, essentially disjoint from the proved regime s>p≥2. The only established local resolution withdraws that entire low-exponent guarantee, which is major mathematical loss for the affected prose claim. No contained, source-supported argument recovers it.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Our main result demonstrates that if the growth rate of a Banach hypothesis space's metric entropy can be bounded by a polynomial function of the radius of the balls, then the hypothesis space can be embedded into a $\mathcal{L}_p$-type Reproducing Kernel Banach space for some $ p \geq 2$.

issues.title: Common-domain mismatch in the main embedding interface

failure_location.quote: Recall that $E$ is an RKBS, so it is a closed subspace of $F=\ell_\infty(X)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof changes the function domain from the quantified Ω to an undeclared X when forming F, the L1 space, and the measure used for theorem:Lpembed. Consequently, those embeddings and the measure-space reduction are not typed as objects belonging to theorem:main.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the main construction does not operate on the common domain specified by the theorem, so the main embedding and the application corollaries lack a well-defined proof interface.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the theorem's quantified domain Ω throughout the appendix interface: write F=ℓ∞(Ω), form the L1 space and measure on Ω, and retain Ω in the evaluation and feature-map construction. The dependent results may then invoke the unchanged theorem.
issues.why_classification: The theorem quantifies Ω, while X has no declared role in this construction; the surrounding function spaces and evaluations uniquely force Ω. This is a repeated identifier substitution that changes no inference, hypothesis, conclusion, rate, or application.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Recall that $E$ is an RKBS, so it is a closed subspace of $F=\ell_\infty(\Omega)$.

issues.title: Isomorphic embedding overstated as isometric

failure_location.quote: and $\hat{E}$ is isometric to $W_{s'}$, a closed subspace of $L_{s'}(\mu)$ by the isometric mapping $i$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof imports norm preservation from theorem:Lpembed even though its stated conclusion supplies only a bounded isomorphism onto a subspace. The stronger isometric premise is therefore unestablished. The subsequent construction needs only the isomorphism and its bounded inverse.
issues.overall_effect: The proof contains an unjustified stronger assertion, but the main embedding conclusion remains obtainable from the weaker isomorphic conclusion actually supplied.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the isometric claim by the isomorphic conclusion actually supplied by theorem:Lpembed. Treat i and i^{-1} as bounded maps and carry their operator-norm constants through the feature-map and embedding estimates; the main embedding statement remains unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old proof makes an unjustified stronger inference, so this is not merely harmless transcription. Nevertheless, the subsequent construction requires only a bounded isomorphism and bounded inverse, making the repair short, local, and routine with no loss of the theorem's substantive guarantee.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: and $\hat{E}$ is isomorphic to $W_{s'}$, a closed subspace of $L_{s'}(\mu)$ by the isomorphic mapping $i$.

issues.title: Main theorem's malformed domain relation
issues.failure_explanation: Reading Ω∈R^d literally makes Ω a point, while E consists of functions on Ω and F is ℓ∞(Ω), both of which require Ω to be the domain set. Thus the theorem's input declaration is ill-typed.
issues.overall_effect: The main theorem's domain hypothesis is malformed, and hence so is the formal basis for its application corollaries, unless the forced subset reading is supplied.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the malformed declaration Ω∈R^d by Ω⊂ℝ^d in the main theorem and its restatement, leaving all other hypotheses and conclusions unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The words “bounded domain,” the functions on Ω, and ℓ∞(Ω) uniquely force Ω to be a subset of ℝ^d rather than a point. The correction is purely transcriptional and automatically restores the same reading for every dependent application.

issues.title: Dudley increment set
issues.failure_explanation: After enlarging the supremum to arbitrary y_i∈E, the set over which it ranges no longer has cardinality controlled by |N_{ε_j}| and |N_{ε_{j-1}}|. Thus the finite-set hypothesis and cardinality term used in the Massart step do not apply to the displayed supremum. The actual increments are g_j(x_i)−g_{j-1}(x_i), which lie in the finite net-difference set.
issues.overall_effect: The old proof does not obtain the claimed Dudley entropy bound at the Massart step, so the Rademacher estimate used by the main embedding theorem and its applications is unsupported at this point.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: At each chaining level define D_j=N_{ε_j}-N_{ε_{j-1}} and retain the supremum only over tuples in D_j^n, rather than enlarging it to arbitrary elements of E. Use |D_j|≤|N_{ε_j}||N_{ε_{j-1}}| and the resulting tuple cardinality in the Massart step; this preserves the Dudley bound and its downstream rate.
issues.why_classification: The old enlargement creates a genuine invalid cardinality inference, so it is not a typo. Undoing that enlargement and counting the actual finite increment tuples is standard local chaining bookkeeping; it requires no new lemma or architecture and causes no loss in the recorded Dudley or embedding guarantees.

issues.title: Massart lemma input structure

failure_location.quote: Let $\mathcal{B}$ be banach space and $A \subset\mathcal{B}$ be a finite set with $r = \max_{a \in A} \|a\|_\BT$

issues.failure_explanation: For the stated input A⊂B, neither the objects a_1,…,a_m as elements of B nor the sum Σ_i σ_i a_i are defined in general. Moreover, the old radius is the norm of a as a single element while the displayed sum requires a tuple of Banach-space vectors. The lemma therefore has an undefined input-output interface.
issues.overall_effect: The generalized Massart estimate cannot be invoked on the chaining tuples under its old statement, so theorem:dudley and the embedding results depending on it lack a well-typed supporting lemma.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the lemma on a finite set A⊂B^m whose elements are tuples a=(a_1,…,a_m), equip those tuples with the component radius r=max_{a∈A,1≤i≤m}||a_i||_B, and use this same tuple convention in the proof and in the invocation on the chaining increments.
issues.why_classification: The old premise does not define the indexed components or their radius, so a genuine interface repair and a check of the invocation are required. The displayed sum, the phrase “components of vector a,” and the chaining application already determine the needed tuple structure, making the repair local and routine without changing the intended estimate or affected conclusions.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a Banach space and $A$ be a finite set of vectors $a=(a_1,...,a_m)$ where $a_i\in \BT$.

issues.title: Inconsistent parameters and scale in the type lemma

failure_location.quote: Let $\tau = s^{-1} - q^{-1}>0$. By the fact that $|U_j|\le m^{k}$, $\|2^kx_i\|_F\le 1$

diagnostic_evidence.quote: then \(\hat{E}=(E,\|\cdot\|_F)\) is of {the} type \(s'\), for each \(1\le s' < p'\).

issues.failure_explanation: The quantities s, q, and τ=s^{-1}-q^{-1} have no declared relation to the lemma's p′ and s′, so the displayed moments do not prove the stated type-s′ inequality. Independently, membership in U_j implies the relevant normalization is 2^j; it does not imply that ‖2^k x_i‖_F≤1 because k indexes |U_j|. Thus the dyadic estimate leading to eq:norm1types does not follow as written.
issues.overall_effect: The type-s′ conclusion used as the geometric input to theorem:main is not derived by the old calculation, leaving the main embedding chain and its applications unsupported at this step.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the lemma's declared parameters consistently by setting τ=1/s′−1/p′>0 and replacing s,q by s′,p′ throughout the moment calculation. For i∈U_j use ||2^j x_i||_F≤1, not the cardinality index k, and recompute the displayed block as 2^{-j}m^{k/p′}=2^{-j}m^{k/s′}m^{-τk}.
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained to the dyadic calculation and preserves the same type-s′ conclusion and all downstream guarantees. It is not a typo under the strict threshold because the old proof explicitly invokes an invalid 2^k normalization and undefined exponents, requiring the calculation to be repaired and checked; however, no new lemma, construction, or substantive weakening is needed.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Let $\tau = 1/s' - 1/p'>0$. Fix a $k$ and a $j \in V_k$, by the fact that $|U_j|\le m^{k}$, $\|2^jx_i\|_F\le 1$
